title: Ten trips to the machine?
hook: Ten items to the machine, one at a time. How far is that?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that every extra trip repeats the whole walk, so carrying one sorted batch covers the distance once instead of once per item

misconception: Carrying things one at a time costs little extra when each trip is short.
objective: For a fixed route and unlimited carrying capacity, one grouped trip pays the distance once instead of once per item. The picture compares repeated travel with a single batch.

recall.question: Six items are 3 m away. You return after every delivery. Carry one per trip, or three per trip: what are the two total distances?
recall.why: Each round trip is 3 + 3 = 6 m. One item per trip requires six trips: 6 × 6 = 36 m. Three per trip requires two trips: 2 × 6 = 12 m. The carrying capacity is stipulated, not measured.
